transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. I guess… I’ve just been a little more stressed than usual. My father-in-law moved in with us, and I’m still keeping it together at work, but at home—and with my coursework—I’m more wound up and short than I like to be. It’s not like I’m falling apart or anything, but I’ve started skipping the things that usually help me clear my head, like fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops. So I figured it might be smart to talk to someone before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
Have you experienced or witnessed any event in the past that felt really overwhelming or traumatic, like an accident, serious injury, or something life-threatening?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, as an EMT I’ve been around some hard situations, but nothing that I’d call, you know, overwhelming or life-threatening to me personally. Nothing like that is really what brought me in, I don’t think.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or interest in doing things that you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking?

Yeah… a bit, I guess. I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest completely or anything, but since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been more wound up at home and with my coursework. Work’s still okay—I’m keeping it together there—but I’ve been shorter than I like to be. And I have been skipping fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops, which usually help me clear my head. It’s probably not a huge thing, but it’s enough that I noticed it.
Have you found that activities like fishing or woodworking don’t bring you the same sense of enjoyment or relief as they used to, even before your father-in-law moved in?

I think before he moved in, those things still helped like they always did. It was more after my father-in-law came to stay with us—about four months ago—that I started noticing the strain. Maybe within the first couple of months, once the home routines and the caregiving stuff kind of became real, I guess. I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s when fishing and woodworking started getting pushed aside more.

When you say you’ve been skipping fishing, woodworking, and the first-aid workshops, is it because you don’t feel like doing them anymore, or is it more that you just don’t have the time or energy with everything else going on?

It’s probably more the time and energy side of it, I think. I still like those things, and usually they help me keep my head clear. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve been keeping it together at work, but at home and with my coursework I’m just more wound up, shorter than I’m used to being… so by the time I could go fishing or work on something, I either don’t make the time or I just feel kind of drained. It’s not that I don’t care about them anymore, if that makes sense.
Have you felt like things you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, just don’t seem as interesting or pleasurable as they used to be?

Not exactly like they’re not pleasurable anymore… I mean, I still think I’d enjoy fishing or woodworking if I got myself to do them. It’s more that since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been holding it together at work, but at home and with my coursework I’m more wound up and short than I’m used to. So I end up skipping the things that usually keep my head clear, like fishing, woodworking, even the first-aid workshops. I guess that probably doesn’t sound ideal, but it feels more like I’m stretched thin than that I’ve stopped liking them.
Have you felt like you don’t get the same satisfaction or enjoyment out of things like fishing or woodworking even when you do manage to do them?

I’m not totally sure, to be honest. The few times I do manage to do them, I think I still get something out of it. Maybe I’m a little distracted or it takes me longer to settle into it, but I wouldn’t say the satisfaction is gone. It’s more that I haven’t been getting to them enough to really know, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more than usual, even when there isn’t a specific problem to solve, like when you’re trying to relax or get ready for bed?

Yeah… I guess I do worry more than I used to, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve just felt more wound up at home and with my coursework. I can keep it together at work, but when I’m supposed to be relaxing, my mind doesn’t settle as easily. And then I end up skipping the things that usually help clear my head, like fishing or woodworking.

Do you find that the worry or feeling wound up stays with you most of the time, even when there isn’t an immediate problem or stressor, like when you’re out of work or your father-in-law doesn’t need anything right then?

Yeah… I think it does hang around some, even when nothing is actively happening. I don’t want to overstate it, because I can still keep it together at work and do what I need to do, but since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’m just more wound up at home than I’m used to.

Even with my coursework, I get shorter and more tense than I’d like. And I’ve been letting the things that usually help me reset—fishing, woodworking, those first-aid workshops—kind of fall off. So… yes, I guess it’s not only when there’s an immediate problem. It’s more like I’m carrying it around, if that makes sense.

Do you find yourself worrying about a variety of things, not just related to your father-in-law or your coursework, like everyday matters or other responsibilities, even when others might not see them as a big deal?

I don’t think so… not in a broad way, anyway. I mean, I probably worry about normal stuff like anyone does, bills or getting things done, but I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly worrying about everything.

It mostly seems tied to what’s been going on at home and trying to keep up with coursework. At least, that’s how it feels to me. If that makes sense.
Have you noticed any physical changes along with feeling wound up, like trouble relaxing, trouble sleeping, feeling tired, trouble focusing, or muscle tension?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed anything major physically. I mean, I can feel wound up, but I don’t want to say I’m having some big sleep problem or anything if that’s not really accurate.

Maybe I have a little harder time settling down sometimes, but… nothing I’ve really been tracking. I’ve just kind of been pushing through it, if that makes sense.
Have you ever felt a sudden rush of intense fear or discomfort that peaked within minutes, like your heart racing, feeling short of breath, or like something terrible is going to happen?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve definitely felt stressed and wound up, but not like a sudden attack where it peaks really fast or I feel like something terrible is happening.

At least, nothing I’d describe that way. Is that what you mean?
Have you felt like you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even when you have the time to do them?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve lost interest in everything, because that’s not really it.

But I have noticed I’m not doing the things that usually help me clear my head. Like fishing, woodworking, even the first-aid workshops I normally like going to… I’ve been skipping those more since my father-in-law moved in and things got more stressful at home. I’m still holding it together at work, but when I do have time, I just don’t seem to follow through like I used to.
When you do get a chance to do things like fishing or woodworking, do you find that they don’t really cheer you up or give you that sense of satisfaction they used to, even a little?

I don’t know that I’d say they don’t cheer me up. When I actually get myself to do them, I think I still can enjoy them some.

It’s more that I haven’t been getting to them, or I kind of talk myself out of it. But I wouldn’t want to overstate it and say there’s no satisfaction there anymore. Does that distinction make sense?
Have you had days where you felt down or unmotivated for most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks or more at a time?

No, I don’t think it’s been like that. I’ve had some low or unmotivated days, sure, but not most of the day nearly every day for two weeks straight.

I mean, I’m still getting up, going to work, doing what I need to do. It’s more… off and on, I guess. I hope that makes sense.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a number of different things, even small or routine matters, not just the situation at home or your coursework?

I don’t think so, not across a bunch of different things. I mean, I can worry like anybody does, but it doesn’t feel like I’m anxious about every little routine matter.

It’s more tied to what’s going on at home, I guess. Maybe I’m not noticing some of it, but I wouldn’t say it’s spread out over everything, if that’s what you mean.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried more often than not, even if it’s not tied to a specific problem or event, like when you’re supposed to be relaxing or going about your day?

Not really, no. I mean, I do get tense or preoccupied sometimes, but I can usually point to what it’s about.

When I’m relaxing or just going through the day, I don’t think I’m sitting there anxious for no reason most of the time. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way. Is that what you’re asking?
Would you say that, overall, you’ve been feeling more anxious or on edge most days, even if it’s not about anything specific, for the past several months?

I’m not sure I’d say most days for several months, no. I mean, I’ve been on edge here and there, but it usually feels like there’s a reason for it, not just out of nowhere.

I don’t want to understate it if you’re hearing something else, but overall I wouldn’t describe myself as anxious most days for no specific reason.
Have you felt like you don’t care about doing the things you used to enjoy, like fishing or woodworking, even when you have the chance to do them?

Yeah… I mean, I still care about those things. It’s not like I’ve lost interest completely.

But I have been skipping them more than I’d like to admit. Fishing, woodworking, even the first-aid workshops I usually enjoy — they normally help clear my head. Since my father-in-law moved in, I’ve just been more wound up at home and with my coursework, and I don’t make the time for them like I used to.

I’m still functioning fine at work, I think, but at home I guess I’m shorter and more tense than I’d prefer. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge when there’s no clear reason or specific stressor, like when things are actually calm at home or at work?

Not usually when things are genuinely calm, no. I mean… I came in because since my father-in-law moved in with us, I’ve been holding it together pretty well at work, but at home and with my coursework I’m more wound up and short than I’m used to.

And I guess I’ve been skipping the things that normally help me clear my head — fishing, woodworking, the first-aid workshops. But it still feels tied to all of that, not like I’m anxious for no reason. Does that answer what you mean?
